notes.title: Steel Mantis Presents - Slain 2: The Beast Within
notes.content:
[h3][b]Steel Mantis [/b]is teaming up with [b]Silver Lining Interactive[/b] to bring you a brand new, blood-soaked, pixel-art action platformer. [/h3]

If you’ve loved [b]Steel Manti[/b]s’ previous titles, you know what’s coming: intense, fast-paced combat, brutal challenges, and an unforgettable story-rich world to explore.

Get ready for [b]Slain 2: The Beast Within[/b], the brutal [b]sequel to Slain: Back From Hell.[/b] The moon is rising, the blood is flowing, and the hunt begins. Step into the boots of [b]Prince Akran, the last of the Wolf Knights[/b], and wield the [b]sentient sword Bathoryn[/b] as you fight through hordes of demonic creatures. Transform into a savage werewolf under the full moon, tear your enemies apart, and reclaim sacred relics in a dark and blood-drenched world consumed by darkness.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/34c383932646329ccb1e88f6294a17747e00a5c1.png[/img]

[h2]What can you expect?[/h2]

[h3]Ferocious Combat[/h3]
If you’ve enjoyed Steel Mantis’ signature fast, satisfying combat, get ready for more of that. Cleave through enemies, unleash elemental chaos with the sentient sword Bathoryn, and feel the rush of every brutal attack.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/24797b9e93ab82f387457e21e72c339ebec168e9.png[/img]

[h3]Blood of Wolf Knights[/h3]
With insane speed and power, you’ll rip through enemies in ways only a cursed knight could. Transform into a savage werewolf under the full moon, and unleash unimaginable speed and power on your enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/083fff5d2bf7ead2a52145b34eaf804b1f7eea31.png[/img]

[h3]Three Deadly Quests[/h3]
Embark on three challenging quests that will test your combat skills, your strategy, and your willpower. Sacrifices must be made, and terrifying foes await at every turn.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/264a10545106378c2074d21cf1fe2e6f7fa808d2.png[/img]

[h3]A World in Ruin[/h3]
Explore haunting, cursed towns, ominous catacombs, and fog-covered highlands - all set in a world that’s teetering on the edge of annihilation.
You know this is a ride you won’t want to miss.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/e5170255b237efda10e59af61719d8ed5f7321c6.png[/img]

[h2][b]Wishlist Now![/b][/h2]

notes.title: CHALLENGE MODE IS HERE!
notes.content:
[h3][i][b]ALL HAIL! The brand new arcade-style Challenge Mode is now available! If you've already beaten the game, Challenge Mode will be ready to play as soon as the latest update has installed. If you haven't beaten the game, Challenge Mode will remain locked until you do! [/b][/i]  [/h3]

These are some of the main differences between Challenge Mode and the default Original Mode:
[list]
[*] Therion is equipped with lives instead of a health bar
[*] Weapons are upgraded on-the-fly by collecting pick-ups
[*] Earn a score by defeating enemies and destroying anything that's destructible
[*] Weapons can be downgraded if you're hit by an enemy
[*] Gain extra lives at score milestones and by collecting Blood of Valfaris
[*] Checkpoints can be destroyed as a way to earn Blood of Valfaris
[/list]
There are more details about Challenge Mode in our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1647920/view/4173228436844477207][b]previous Steam post[/b][/url].

We've discounted the game to celebrate the arrival of Challenge Mode – it's available for half-price until next Monday, 2nd September.

[b]VALFARIS: MECHA THERION ARRIVES ON CONSOLES LATER THIS WEEK![/b]

The wait is almost over! You'll be able to grab Valfaris: Mecha Therion on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation, and Xbox consoles in just a few days! It launches 29th August. Be sure to add the game to your wishlist on the console of your choice and you'll be notified as soon as it's available.

notes.title: CHALLENGE MODE COMING SOON – HERE'S WHAT TO EXPECT!
notes.content:
[h3][b]Challenge Mode is coming in a free update to Valfaris: Mecha Therion on 26th August. Designed to give skilled players another way to play through the game, Challenge Mode includes some arcade-style changes, such as lives instead of health, a scoring system, and weapon upgrades via pick-ups.[/b][/h3]

[h3][b]Challenge Mode details:[/b][/h3]

[b]Score[/b]
[list]
[*] Increase your score by killing enemies and destroying anything that's destructible!
[*] Defeat bosses quickly for bonus points
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/8a78aab9e7744d527ac9158f572a8c48970c88bb.gif[/img]

[b]Lives + Checkpoints[/b]
[list]
[*] Number of current lives are represented by red bars on the HUD
[*] Start with 2x lives. Lose a life when you take a hit 
[*] Lose all lives and you restart from the last checkpoint
[*] When you respawn at a checkpoint, 1x life is deducted from the total lives you had when the checkpoint was activated e.g. if you activate a checkpoint with 3x lives and then subsequently lose all those 3x lives, you respawn at that checkpoint with 2x Lives. It's game over when you have 0x lives left 
[*] Gain extra lives at score increments, starting at 100,000 and then every 120,000 after that i.e. 100,000 / 220,000 / 360,000
[*] You also gain an extra life for every 5x Blood of Valfaris you collect
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/1f2db4e0157766bdfa09cf64f5555c198e0f7d3c.gif[/img]
[list]

[*] Score multiplier increases with your current amount of lives: 2x Lives = 1.0 Multiplier / 3x Lives = 1.2 Multiplier / 4x Lives = 1.4 / 5x Lives = 1.6
[*] Destroying a checkpoint yields 1x Blood of Valfaris. Only melee attacks can destroy a checkpoint
[*] WARNING: You can't utilise a destroyed checkpoint
[*] Weapon and Module loadouts can still be changed at checkpoints
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/e9b5b648930ce4805d198ef8d252fc53632cb0c1.gif[/img]

[b]Upgrades[/b]
[list]
[*] Weapons are no longer upgraded at checkpoints 
[*] Defeated enemies can drop weapon pick-ups. Collect these to upgrade your Destroyer, Melee, and Auxiliary weapons 
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/665baeddb52771ee232bd90f3e68a3d550b20456.gif[/img]
[list]
[*] Weapon ranks are displayed on the HUD 
[*] As well as losing a life, taking a hit can also downgrade weapons
[/list]
All hail Challenge Mode - we hope you enjoy it!

[b]Matt | [url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/BigSugar]Big Sugar[/url][/b]

notes.title: Version 1.0.5 is here! Weapon adjustments & Performance Improvements
notes.content:
The Galaxy has been ripped a new wormhole that leads straight to version 1.0.5! We've had some weapon & module adjustments, overall performance improvements, and added in Polish localization! 

[b]WEAPONS[/b]

[i]Electroburst[/i]
[list]
[*] Now charges more quickly.
[*] No longer slows down your movement while charging.
[/list]

[i]Wrath of Kykris[/i]
[list]
[*] No longer destroys plasma projectiles (it will still destroy solid ones like missiles).
[*] Uses more energy to fire.
[*] Small damage nerf.
[/list]

[b]MODULES[/b]

[i]Reflector Edge[/i]
[list]
[*] Increased damage of reflected projectiles.
[*] Increased number of types of projectiles that can be reflected.
[/list]

[i]Crash-Burst[/i]
[list]
[*] Now unleashes banshee ghosts on impact.
[/list]

The [i]Rally[/i] module has been replaced with the "[i]Fuel Stabiliser[/i]" module.
This module reduces the fuel cost to boost, allowing you to perform 3 boosts when the fuel gauge is full, rather than 2.

[b]OTHER CHANGES:[/b]
- Added in Polish language.
- Performance improvements.

notes.title: STARTER GUIDE TO GET YOU READY FOR LAUNCH DAY!
notes.content:
[h3][i][b]With the release of Valfaris: Mecha Therion fast-approaching (it launches 21st November), we thought it would be useful to cover some of the basics to get you prepped for blast off![/b][/i][/h3]

[h3][b]THERION'S STORY CONTINUES...[/b][/h3]
In his pursuit of the evil Lord Vroll (which began in the previous game, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/600130/Valfaris/]Valfaris[/url]), Therion has travelled to the edge of the edge, where the unholy flourish, and the sadistic revel in demonic pleasures. His thirst for retribution unsated, Therion wields a new weapon, a behemoth suit forged of metal. Encased within it's giant frame, he becomes the machine's beating heart and its vengeful rage.

[i]SUIT-UP AND UNLEASH MECHA HELL![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/1a9cfe216df75a0ab9e020791d7f728d8c87af95.png[/img]

[h3][b]DESTROYER WEAPONS [/b][/h3]
This class of weapon is the mecha suit's primary armament. There are a total of six different Destroyers available, although you only start with the Hellwraith – a powerful minigun that fires tormented souls. Using the equipped Destroyer at maximum firepower uses suit energy. If energy is completely depleted, the Destroyer's firepower is greatly reduced. 

[h3][b]MELEE WEAPONS[/b][/h3]
Formidable close-quarters weapons, although the suit's blade serves a greater purpose than merely slicing through enemies. It can also be used against projectiles, debris, and parts of the environment. Using the Melee weapon yields energy, which is absorbed into the suit and converted into firepower for the Destroyer weapon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/92badc5c08ae2ec5dada691ee21a5e3ac5b44ea8.gif[/img]
[i]Destroyer, Melee, and Auxiliary weapons being used in rapid succession[/i]

[h3][b]AUXILIARY WEAPONS[/b][/h3]
Supporting the suit's Destroyer and Melee weapons, the additional offensive options provided by Auxiliary attachments shouldn't be overlooked. As with Destroyers, using Auxiliary weapons depletes the suit's energy. Initially, the suit is equipped with Blade Tempest, which fires a barrage of homing blades that can eliminate multiple targets.

[h3][b]HUD INDICATORS[/b][/h3]
There's more to piloting the mecha than just using the Destroyer to mindlessly blast enemies. If you want to survive, you'll need to keep an eye on the HUD. Being aware of the various indicators is fundamental to utilising the suit's capabilities and mastering the art of switching between your equipped weapons for maximum combat effectiveness.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/c87791218124192be9933805b4fd90e3b6e50261.png[/img]

[h3][b]MODULES[/b][/h3]
Utility add-ons that upgrade the suit's capabilities. For example, if you boost into a solid object with the Crash-Burst Module equipped, the suit unleashes a damaging shockwave. The mecha suit can be upgraded with a maximum of three Module slots.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/f20d3104e266b885e7b6682004a197b0df942598.png[/img]
[i]Modules can be found in secret areas or are sometimes awarded for defeating certain enemies[/i] 

[h3][b]HYPERCORE[/b][/h3]
A powerful energy source that augments a Destroyer weapon's effectiveness when it's equipped. For example, with the Hypercore fitted, the Hellwraith is enhanced with up to three skulls which orbit the suit and provide extra firepower.    

[h3][b]BOOSTING[/b][/h3]
A valuable mobility feature that requires Boost Fuel and gives the suit a temporary surge of forward thrust. When active, the suit is impervious to damage, so you can boost to break through parts of the environment or burst through a wave of enemies without losing health. Boosting into enemies also activates the suit's Critical Strike – a devastating blow from the Melee weapon that deals a large amount of damage. Once depleted, Boost Fuel automatically replenishes over time. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/9bb31204fb495286524ca6d4856cc2cd03048580.gif[/img]
[i]Don't just use Boost to smash through blockages – get in the habit of using it to perform Critical Strikes[/i]

[h3][b]CHECKPOINTS[/b][/h3]
If the suit's health becomes fully depleted, you'll respawn at the most recently activated checkpoint. To activate a checkpoint, simply fly over it. Activating a checkpoint auto-fills the suit's health, energy, and boost fuel. Docking at a checkpoint allows you to adjust the suit's weapon and module loadout, and also use Blood Metal to upgrade your weapons. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/a006ab001969dc884def293e7c84bb53f752343c.gif[/img]
[i]Most weapons can be upgraded to Rank 4[/i] 

[h3][b]BLOOD METAL[/b][/h3]
The currency used to upgrade the suit's weapons. One new Blood Metal is acquired every time the Blood Gauge is filled, which is achieved in a number of ways, such as killing enemies and destroying projectiles. The Blood Gauge fills faster if you successfully destroy a complete wave of enemies. Filling the Blood Gauge also increases the threat level, and when the gauge flashes red there's a high probability a Champion enemy will appear. 

[i]And that pretty much covers the basics – you're ready to suit-up on launch day! [/i]

[h3][b]VALFARIS: MECHA THERION WALLPAPERS[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/f32c8947af7e43dee7e0bcb9afdd6c5e28d9fcff.png[/img]

[*] Various bug fixes
[/list]
The biggest change is the addition of the manual turn ability, which allows the player to turn 180 and fire in the opposite direction. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/37caecabfaa3088e3f42e4ef0d1848e90d399392.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/d95a3f2774c9c10f68afd4c65c0bd4d0768d6664.gif[/img]

Previously, the mech would only auto-turn in specific situations, but the option to turn manually was frequently requested, so now players can choose between auto and manual turning in the options menu. It allows for more freedom and control over how to deal with incoming threats, regardless of which side of the screen they're coming from. 

Overall, we feel the playtest has achieved its main objective – to help make the game even better! The final tweaks and added polish are going great and we'll be able to confirm a release date very soon, so stay tuned!

Matt | Big Sugar

Lord Vroll is our series villain – he's a murderous tyrant, powerful [i]and[/i] power-hungry. He previously appeared as the big bad in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/369070/Slain_Back_from_Hell/]Slain: Back From Hell[/url], where he transformed into a dragon before making his escape. And while Vroll never actually appeared in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/600130/Valfaris/]Valfaris[/url] (the sequel to Slain: Back From Hell), the aftermath of his presence was stark and permeated every corner as Therion doggedly followed his trail.

Lord Vroll returns in Valfaris: Mecha Therion and it's up to Therion (who also happens to be Vroll's son) to finally confront his father for a final, epic showdown.

notes.title: DEMO IS LIVE NOW!
notes.content:
[h3][b]The very first Valfaris: Mecha Therion demo is now live and available to download from the game's Steam page![/b][/h3]

Here's what you can do in the demo:

[list]
[*] Play through the tutorial
[*] Play through the entire second stage, 'Ruins of Anvin'
[*] Try three of the Destroyer class weapons (Hellwraith, Hellhammer, Bringer of Mayhem)
[*] Try two of the Melee class weapons (Bathoryn, Therion's Fist)
[*] Try three of the Auxiliary class weapons (Homing Swords, Electroburst, Bunker-Buster)
[*] Try two of the Module unit suit power-ups (Reaper, Crash-Burst)
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41116270/54c7d6b456c2bfc690c0585c6fa25eba06ce10d9.gif[/img]

It's also worth mentioning that weapons can be upgraded — simply land at a checkpoint and select the 'Upgrade' option. If you have enough resources, you'll be able to increase the rank of the selected weapon. You start the demo with a stash of 30 Blood Metals, which will allow you to upgrade one of your weapons at the very first checkpoint if you want to.

On the first attempt, a single playthrough of the demo will take most players between 15 and 30 minutes.  However, it's very much designed with multiple playthroughs in mind, so you can try the different weapon loadouts (and also find a couple of small secret areas). 

If you play the demo and have any feedback, please go ahead and drop it here: [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1647920/discussions/0/3757726349616134013/]Demo Feedback[/url][/b]

Thanks for playing!

notes.title: Hellish pixel platformer Valfaris goes 2.5D in forthcoming sequel
notes.content: Valfaris was a sumptuous metal-themed 2D platformer with some of the most impressive pixel art this side of Owlboy. The work of Slain studio Steel Mantis, it was a bonkers modern take on classic action-platformers like Shadow of the Beast. Now it's getting a sequel called Valfaris: Mecha Therion that mixes things up a bit... Read more.

notes.title: VALFARIS: MECHA THERION – FIRST TRAILER AND DETAILS!
notes.content:
Welcome to the Steam page for Valfaris: Mecha Therion – a new side-scrolling shoot 'em up from developer Steel Mantis, and sequel to the studio's previous game, Valfaris. It's still early in development and won't be out until late 2022 for PC and consoles, but you can expect an action-packed shmup with a challenging, old-school feel, crunchy low-poly visuals, and gore galore!

Take a look at the reveal trailer:
[previewyoutube=cKxyAJM7g-0;full][/previewyoutube]
If you played Valfaris and are interested to know why Steel Mantis wanted to switch from action-platformer to shmup for the sequel, programmer and designer Thomas Jenns discusses it in a [b][url=https://blog.playstation.com/2021/08/25/valfaris-sequel-switches-genres-but-stays-true-to-its-roots/]post on the Playstation Blog.[/url][/b]

We're looking forward to sharing more Valfaris: Mecha Therion info with you soon!

Matt | Big Sugar
